# Tips for New Users

## Common FLOWCAL Terminology

#### Time-Related

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1696" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Business Month">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Business Month</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Business Month">

The business month is the first month after the last close. If the last month closed is April and it is July 10, the business month is May (last month after close in April).

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1697" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Data Resolution">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Data Resolution</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Data Resolution">

Defines whether the flow data will be captured in 15-minute, hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly records. This is defined at the meter level, by setting the Data Resolution field within the meter’ characteristics.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1698" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Datetime Effective">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Datetime Effective</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Datetime Effective">

Records with a start date and time and an end date and time; may span all of time.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1699" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Effective Date">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Effective Date / Effective End Date</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Effective Date">

Time stamp that signifies when the meter acquired the data. The effective date is the beginning time for which the record is effective. The end date indicates the end time for which the record is effective.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1701" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="GMS Date">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />GMS Date</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="GMS Date">

Gas measurement system day on which a database record was created or last modified.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1702" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Measurement Month">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Measurement Month</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Measurement Month">

A one-month period with start and end dates defined by a contract day and contract hour; generally, offset from the corresponding calendar month because of the contract day and hour.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Measurement Month">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

A meter has a contract day of 5 and a contract hour of 7; in this case, the measurement month begins January 5th at 7 a.m. and ends February 5th at 7 a.m.; note that the first four days of February are included in the January measurement month.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1703" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Start End Date">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Start / End date</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Start End Date">

Datetime for when the data starts and ends.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1705" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Time Leads">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Time Leads vs. Time Trails data</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Time Leads">

Proprietary term indicating where an interval of time is recorded within the beginning and ending timestamps. This is defined at the meter level, by setting the Data Span field within the meter characteristics.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Time Leads">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

The period of 1:00 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. is either labeled at the 13:00 hour (time leads data) or the 14:00 hour (time trails data) in the computer logs.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1707" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Timestamp">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Timestamp</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Timestamp">

A date and time expressed as an integer and representing the number of seconds elapsed since 12/31/1969 @ 18:00:00. Time zones and Daylight Saving Time are not considered.

</div>

#### Data-Related

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1708" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Correlation Factor">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Correlation Factor (also known as VCF and CF)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Correlation Factor">

A factor used to compensate for the inherent inaccuracy associated with calculating volumes from averages of the flowing parameters as opposed to the actual instantaneous values used by the original flow-computing device. This factor is only required for recalculation purposes, but it is also useful as a validation parameter and is a term unique to the FLOWCAL system. Ideally, the VCF calculated by FLOWCAL will be at or near 1.0.

For more information, see: Understanding Correlation Factors for Liquid Meters and Understanding Volume Correlation Factors for Gas Meters.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1711" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Exception">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Exception</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Exception">

Exceptions are created when suspect data for a meter, location or quality source is imported or added as an edit.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1712" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Measured v Standard">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Measured Conditions versus Standard Conditions</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Measured v Standard">

**Measured** - Volume is shown at the meter pressure base and temperature base.

**Standard** - Volume shown at the system pressure base, temperature base, and system units.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1714" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Original v Current">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Original Data versus Current Data</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Original v Current">

**Original** - Original data import from the field, which imports into FLOWCAL as revision 0.

**Current **- Current data is the most current record revision.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example-Original Data">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

A record is imported and is original data from the field, which is stored as revision 0. The user applies an analysis to the record and it is recalculated. The edited record is stored as revision 1. Revision 1 is the current data record. Revision 0 remains the original data record.

</div>

 

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1716" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Rollups">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Rollups or Final Form Data</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Rollups">

Process by which hourly or 15-minute numbers are summed or averaged to get an hourly, daily, and monthly total or average used for reporting. This is done by FLOWCAL's meter and location rollups services.

</div>

#### Feature-Related

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1718" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Fluid Phase">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Fluid Phase</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Fluid Phase">

Refers to the type of product the meter measured. FLOWCAL supports two fluid phases: gas and liquid. Gas is used for meters flowing products such as natural gas and helium. Liquid is used for meters flowing products such as crude oil, NGL, Y-grade, and refined products.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1719" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Lists v Locations">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Lists versus Locations versus Close Groups</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Lists v Locations">

Lists are used to create logical combinations of meters, locations, and quality sources for importing, viewing, and exporting data, and generating reports. Lists are not datetime effective.

Locations are used in FLOWCAL for many reasons, including calculating total volume, energy and mass for multiple meters; calculating lost and unaccounted for volume, energy, and mass such as on a pipeline segment; calculating inventory. Locations are the basis for tanks, liquid caverns, and gas inventory locations; comparison locations allow for comparing a meter to another meter, a location to another location or a location to a meter.

Close groups are date-effective groups of meters that allow the user to close meters in bulk. Meters can only belong to one close group at a time.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1722" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Reports v Exports">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Reports versus Exports</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Reports v Exports">

Reports are created with Crystal Reports and are access from the Standard Reports screen. Reports can be previewed in the Crystal Viewer that is standard with FLOWCAL and can be exported to several different formats, such as PDF.

Exports are typically made available through DLL files to export data. Running an export often generates a file such as XLS, which can be further manipulated. FLOWCAL ships with several standard exports, which can be accessed from the Export menu.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1724" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="System v Application">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />System versus Application</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="System v Application">

System-level settings allows a user to manage security for users, groups, and objects within each system independently. Users can also configure many system- specific settings such as System Factors, System Units, System Options, and Rollup Options. This is a powerful tool that allows a user to have several systems within one database. By default, FLOWCAL ships with one system called Enterprise.

There is no limit as to the number of systems that can be created and because security is defined within each system, one user could have full access to one system and its objects and no access or read-only access to another.

The application settings are a level higher than systems in that application settings affect all systems, like Service Configuration.

</div>

#### Import-Related

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1726" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="CFX">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />CFX</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="CFX">

Proprietary binary file format to bring flow data and configuration information from meters into FLOWCAL.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1727" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="PFX">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />PFX</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="PFX">

Proprietary binary file format used to bring meter prove data from liquid meters into FLOWCAL and PROVEit.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1728" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="TFX">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />TFX</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="TFX">

Proprietary binary file format to bring volume and accounting information from run tickets and gauge tickets (pipelines, LACTs, trucks, rail cars, marine vessels, or tank tickets) into FLOWCAL.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" id="kanchor1729" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Transaction Queue">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Transaction Queue (TQ)</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Transaction Queue">

The Transaction Queue service (FcSrvTrans.exe) is a Windows service that can be installed on the application server to import data into FLOWCAL on a near real-time basis. The Transaction Queue consists of two database tables (FC\_ TRANSACTION_QUEUE and FC_TRANSACTION_SNAPSHOT) to which external processes insert rows corresponding to various transactions.

</div>
